stages.title: Labour market: demand for labour
stages.sub: Explain why firms hire labour, what makes that demand elastic or inelastic, and how this plays out in the gig economy.

steps.q: A café sells more coffee because a new office block opens nearby. What happens to the number of baristas the café wants to hire?
steps.hint: Think about why the café needs staff at all: is it for its own sake, or because of something else?

steps.right: No, it becomes more cautious about hiring
steps.wrong: Yes, hiring stays just as strong

steps.right: Buys the machine and cuts staff
steps.wrong: Keeps the same staff and ignores the machine
steps.hint: Firms compare the cost of workers against the cost of the alternative that could do the same job.

steps.q: At the roastery, staff can easily be swapped for a machine. At a hospital, nurses are very hard to replace with machines. If wages rise 10% at each, where will the fall in staff hired be bigger?
steps.right: At the roastery, where substitution is easy
steps.wrong: At the hospital, where substitution is hard
steps.hint: Where is it easier for the employer to react to the wage rise by switching to something else?

steps.q: A delivery firm hires riders only when it has jobs for them, with no guaranteed hours. What does this give both the firm and the rider, compared with a fixed 9-to-5 job?
steps.right: More flexibility over when work happens
steps.hint: Think about what changes when hours are not fixed in advance.

steps.q: That same rider has no guaranteed hours and no sick pay. If deliveries dry up one week, what happens to their income?
steps.right: It can drop sharply with no safety net
steps.wrong: It stays steady because of guaranteed pay
steps.hint: Without fixed hours, what protects the rider's earnings in a quiet week?

steps.q: Weighing up the flexibility firms and riders gain against the insecurity riders face, what kind of debate does this style of work create?
steps.right: A trade-off between flexibility and insecurity
steps.wrong: A settled matter with no real downside
steps.hint: Does the flexibility come free, or does it come alongside a cost for workers?
